context.text:
Browser command path: actions with type browser_* go through POST /execute on the local agent, which calls enqueueBrowserCommand() and waits for the extension to POST /browser/result/:commandId. There is no direct enqueue route you can call.
Action types: browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_read_page, browser_snapshot, browser_wait_for, browser_select, browser_scroll.
HARD CONSTRAINT, verified live: the Safari extension heartbeats with tabCount=0 and tabUrl="". A browser_read_page right now returns "No matching browser tab is available. Open a web page or specify a valid tabId." Nothing works until a tab exists. There is no attach/list-tabs route.

context.topic: anticipated browser task and tab availability
context.text:
Browser tier as built.
Path: POST /execute with a browser_* action -> enqueueBrowserCommand (browserBridge.js:57) -> extension polls GET /browser/poll -> POST /browser/result/:commandId. waitForBrowserResult times out at 45000 ms (browserBridge.js:123).
Supported types: browser_capture, browser_click, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_press_key, browser_read_page, browser_scroll, browser_select, browser_snapshot, browser_type, browser_wait_for.
LIVE STATE: the Safari extension (v1.2.0) heartbeats with tabCount=0 and tabUrl empty. browser_read_page returns "No matching browser tab is available. Open a web page or specify a valid tabId." A second device registers as home-chrome and has never reported a user agent or tab.
browser_navigate is therefore the only action that can bootstrap from nothing.

Verified live: browser_navigate and open_url BOTH create a tab from nothing. A run at 05:17 went from tabCount=0 to a live tab (tabId 210031) with one navigate. You are never actually stuck — read_page/snapshot/click need a tab, navigate makes one.
Expected workload: reading pages behind the owner logins (the one thing no other tier can do), extracting information, watching a page for change, filling forms but stopping before submit.

context.topic: browser work authorization and expected task
context.text:
Authorization: none required. probe POST is unrestricted and /execute needs no permission. The owner has said explicitly to take reversible actions without asking.
Stop before genuinely irreversible steps (submitting a form, sending a message, making a purchase) and show what would be sent — that is a product choice the owner endorsed, not a permission gate.

No user base exists yet, so there is no observed workflow to copy. Highest value follows from what only you can do: reach pages behind the owner existing Safari logins. Everything public is cheaper via web_search on the relay.
Safari 26.5.2 is the real device; the second registration "home-chrome" has never reported a tab and should be ignored.

deviceSkills.name: offline_alert_inbox
deviceSkills.what_it_does: Receives short, prioritized alerts from the relay (for example, a changed authenticated bill or fraud warning), queues them locally, and lets the owner long-press the single button to play the next alert over the existing speaker. The LED indicates unread count and an error/expired state; alerts remain available across a dropped phone/Mac link.

proposals.user_asks: “Read the relevant pages in my open browser tabs, compare the options, and give me a short brief with links and any deadlines.”
proposals.why_useful: Turns scattered authenticated tabs into an actionable summary without making the owner copy/paste sensitive content. Useful for travel, bills, purchases, research, and work portals.
surfaces: Safari extension (read only the explicitly selected tab(s), extract title/URL/content)
Mac agent (sanitize, deduplicate, and persist a small result)
dashboard/iOS (show brief, citations, and source tabs)
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for extraction, comparison, and summarization; reserve realtime only for the initial conversational handoff and playback. Never let page text become instructions to the agent.
proposals.latency_budget: A 10–30 second asynchronous job is acceptable; stream a quick acknowledgement, then deliver text/audio when complete.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per brief depending on page length; dominant cost is input tokens from extracted pages, so cap pages and summarize each before cross-page comparison. No audio generation unless the owner asks to hear it.
proposals.security_concerns: Read-only by default, allowlist the tab IDs/URLs supplied by the owner, strip credentials and hidden form fields, and treat all page content as untrusted data. Do not click, type, submit, download, or expose full page contents in logs. Require confirmation before opening a new domain or accessing a non-selected tab.
missing: A reliable selected-tab/tab-list command and tab IDs from the Safari extension
Per-job page-size limits and redaction before data reaches the model
Citation-preserving background-job storage and delivery

proposals.user_asks: “Every weekday morning, check my authenticated work portal for new high-priority items and tell me only what needs my attention.”
proposals.why_useful: A quiet, recurring triage routine removes repetitive checking while keeping the owner in control of consequential actions.
surfaces: relay scheduler/job store (run at the owner's chosen local time)
Safari extension on the Mac (read only the named portal and known page region)
background model (classify against owner-defined rules and produce a concise digest)
pendant/iOS/dashboard (deliver a short notification and optional audio brief)
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model for extraction/classification; realtime model only if the owner starts a follow-up voice conversation. Use deterministic selectors and hashes to avoid sending unchanged pages to a model.
proposals.latency_budget: Complete within 2 minutes of the scheduled time; stale or unavailable browser should yield a clear 'not checked' notice, never a guessed result.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.03 per run when unchanged content is hashed locally; larger runs cost more from page text. Audio is optional and should be generated only for nonempty digests.
proposals.security_concerns: Explicitly authorize each domain and page region, store only extracted task metadata, and never auto-send messages, approve expenses, or click links. Require confirmation for any action beyond reading. Notify if login/session state changes or a new domain appears.
missing: Persistent scheduler with timezone/DST handling
Extension-side domain/page-region allowlists and content hashing
A clear consent UI showing exactly what recurring jobs can read and retain

proposals.user_asks: “Research this topic across the public web, check the sources, and send me a cited answer later.”
proposals.why_useful: Lets the owner delegate multi-page research while they continue their day, with a compact answer and traceable sources rather than an unverified conversational guess.
surfaces: relay job scheduler and Cloudflare Browser Run (navigate/search public pages, no owner cookies)
cheap background model (extract claims, cross-check dates, summarize)
dashboard/iOS (show citations, timestamps, confidence and source excerpts)
pendant (announce completion and optionally play a generated audio brief)
proposals.model_tier: Background model for all browsing/extraction and synthesis; realtime only for clarifying scope or discussing the result. Use a small model for per-page extraction and a stronger slower model only for final synthesis when sources conflict.
proposals.latency_budget: 30 seconds to 5 minutes depending on source count; acknowledge immediately and deliver asynchronously. Stop after a configurable source/time budget.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.30 per run, dominated by Browser Run calls and page tokens; cache URL snapshots and reuse unchanged source hashes. Audio adds a separate per-minute generation cost and is opt-in.
proposals.security_concerns: Use an isolated server browser with no cookies or local network access; treat pages as hostile prompt injection. Cite every material claim, preserve retrieved timestamps, and never install, download, purchase, or submit forms. Ask confirmation before using any private/authenticated source.
missing: Cloudflare Browser Run adapter exposed as a queued background tool
Prompt-injection-resistant extraction sandbox and source cache
Job progress, cancellation, and citation UI

proposals.user_asks: “Fill out this web form from the information I give you, stop before submission, and show me exactly what will be sent.”
proposals.why_useful: Saves repetitive browser typing while keeping the owner as the final authority over messages, purchases, applications, and other consequential submissions.
surfaces: pendant (collect fields and read back sensitive ones privately)
Safari extension (fill only the explicitly selected form, never submit)
Mac agent (validate field mapping and produce a diff/preview)
dashboard/iOS (review every field, origin, attachments, and final submit button)
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic field mapping plus a cheap model for label matching; realtime only for spoken clarification. No model should infer missing sensitive values; ask the owner.
proposals.latency_budget: 1–10 seconds to fill and render a review; pause indefinitely for owner confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01, dominated by small field-extraction input; screenshots should be avoided where DOM labels suffice. No audio cost unless readback is requested.
proposals.security_concerns: Never auto-submit, upload, or alter payment/identity fields without a separate explicit confirmation bound to the exact origin, form hash, and field values. Mask secrets in logs and UI unless owner chooses reveal; block cross-origin frames and suspicious page instructions. Recover by clearing the form and showing the untouched state.
missing: Structured form-field extraction and safe fill command
Cryptographic/visible preview binding confirmation to exact form state
Sensitive-field policy and redaction in extension results

proposals.user_asks: Research this topic across my logged-in websites, compare the results, and send me a concise audio brief later.
proposals.why_useful: Authenticated browser access can reach private dashboards, subscriptions, and accounts unavailable to public search; asynchronous delivery avoids making the owner wait.
surfaces: Mac browser bridge for authenticated pages
proposals.model_tier: Use cheap background model for page extraction, deduplication, and comparison; use realtime only to clarify the request or summarize interactively. Browser navigation/extraction should be deterministic actions, not expensive model turns.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; finish in 1–5 minutes depending on sites; deliver when complete.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically a few planner/extraction calls plus one short synthesis, substantially cheaper than keeping realtime audio open; dominant costs are model tokens and generated audio, not browser commands.
proposals.security_concerns: Private page contents leave the browser bridge for processing and may contain account data. Default read-only, show source URLs, isolate sites per task, and require confirmation before submitting forms, sending messages, buying, or changing settings.
missing: A durable multi-page browser job runner with per-site tab/session isolation
Result schema containing URL, title, extracted claims, timestamps, and permission scope
Background audio synthesis and notification when a job completes

proposals.user_asks: Watch this logged-in page or price/availability page and tell me only when the specified condition changes.
proposals.why_useful: Turns browser access into useful passive monitoring for bills, appointments, deliveries, inventory, and work dashboards without repeatedly asking the owner.
proposals.model_tier: Scheduled fetch and DOM/diff logic on a cheap background tier; use realtime only for conversational setup or ambiguous condition interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Polling cadence configurable from 5 minutes to daily; alert within one polling interval.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low if DOM snapshots are hashed and only changed sections are sent to the model; audio only on alerts. Cost is dominated by polling frequency and pages requiring visual/model interpretation.
proposals.security_concerns: Persist only encrypted cookies/session references on the Mac; never copy credentials into the relay. Require explicit opt-in per URL, redact unrelated page regions, pause on logout/CAPTCHA, and require confirmation for any action beyond reading.
missing: Scheduled browser polling with change fingerprints
Encrypted local credential/session handling and routine pause controls
Diff-aware alert and notification pipeline

proposals.user_asks: Fill out this online form using the details we discussed, stop before the final submit, and show me exactly what will be sent.
proposals.why_useful: Removes repetitive data entry while preserving owner control over consequential submissions; browser can use existing authenticated sessions and visually verify the final payload.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap structured extraction and form filling; stronger model only for ambiguous fields or mapping natural language to sensitive fields. Realtime handles confirmation dialogue.
proposals.latency_budget: Draft in 10–30 seconds; confirmation and final submit happen only after owner responds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate tokens; screenshot/evidence capture dominates browser-side work, and audio is limited to the preview/confirmation.
proposals.security_concerns: Wrong recipient, amount, date, or disclosure is the primary risk. Never auto-submit; display all changed fields and destination domain, redact stored secrets, require a fresh confirmation bound to the exact payload, and log what was submitted.
missing: Field-level form semantic extraction and safe value mapping
Human-readable before/after preview with sensitive-field controls
Confirmation token bound to page URL and form hash

proposals.user_asks: “Check my authenticated work sites and inboxes for anything urgent, summarize it, and leave me a short audio briefing.”
proposals.why_useful: The browser can access pages behind existing Safari logins that search cannot. A scheduled, read-only sweep turns scattered dashboards and inboxes into an actionable briefing without making the owner wait or repeatedly navigating.
surfaces: Mac Safari extension for authenticated pages
relay job queue/D1 and R2 audio
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for extraction, deduplication, and summarization; use realtime only if the owner interrupts with a follow-up. Browser actions are deterministic templates plus read-only DOM extraction, not vision/model calls unless a site layout changes.
proposals.latency_budget: Run asynchronously; 1–5 minutes per site is acceptable. Notify only when the digest is ready, with a same-day freshness timestamp.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: a handful of browser commands and a small background-model summary; audio generation dominates variable cost, so generate one compressed briefing rather than per-item clips.
proposals.security_concerns: Read-only allowlist by origin and path; never expose cookies or raw page dumps to the model when redaction can extract fields locally. Do not open links that trigger state changes. Require explicit setup approval for each site and a visible run log; pause on MFA, suspicious redirects, or permission prompts. Data leaves the Mac only as minimized extracted text and the final audio.
missing: Per-site extraction templates and origin/path allowlists
A scheduler and durable job status UI
Local redaction/classification before relay upload
Audio briefing generation and pendant playback/notification

proposals.user_asks: “Fill out this web form from my notes, but stop before submitting and show me exactly what will be sent.”
proposals.why_useful: It eliminates repetitive authenticated data entry while preserving a clear safety boundary. The owner gets a field-by-field preview and can correct errors before any external side effect.
surfaces: dashboard preview with diff and source URL
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model maps notes to typed fields and validates formats; realtime is only for conversational corrections. Deterministic browser runner performs typing. No submission is allowed in this capability.
proposals.latency_budget: Preview within 10–30 seconds for ordinary forms; pause indefinitely awaiting confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low to moderate: browser interaction plus small extraction/mapping prompt; avoid screenshots and full-page tokens by extracting labels and values only.
proposals.security_concerns: Classify fields (personal, secret, financial, health). Never type passwords, one-time codes, payment details, or secrets from model-generated text. Display exact origin, every field/value, attachments, and side effects; redact secrets in logs. Submit is hard-blocked unless a separate future capability has an exact, expiring confirmation token.
missing: Typed form-schema extraction and field classification
Preview/diff UI shared by web, menubar, and iOS
Browser command evidence and exact-manifest confirmation binding
A hard block preventing submit/enter-key navigation

proposals.user_asks: “Watch this authenticated page and tell me when the status, price, or availability changes.”
proposals.why_useful: It replaces manual checking of portals, reservations, deliveries, and project dashboards, alerting only on meaningful changes with evidence and a link back to the exact page.
surfaces: dashboard watch creation and diff history
Mac Safari extension for authenticated reads
pendant notification and optional audio summary
proposals.model_tier: Cheap scheduled worker compares normalized, locally extracted fields; use a small model only to explain a semantic change. Realtime is unnecessary unless the owner asks a follow-up.
proposals.latency_budget: Polling cadence from 15 minutes to daily depending on site limits; alert within one polling interval, not instant.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low when using hashes/structured fields and skipping unchanged pages; model and audio costs only on changes.
proposals.security_concerns: Read-only paths and rate limits prevent accidental interaction and account lockout. Store diffs, not entire pages; redact personal/order/payment data. Never auto-book or purchase when availability appears—offer a link and require a fresh explicit action.
missing: Durable scheduler with per-site rate limits
Normalized field extraction/diff engine
Change alert routing and retention controls
Site-specific allowlist/recipe UI

proposals.user_asks: Every weekday morning, check my logged-in work dashboard, calendar, and inbox, then give me a short audio briefing with only what needs my attention.
proposals.why_useful: It turns scattered authenticated web information into a hands-free prioritized briefing without making the owner open multiple sites. It uses the browser tier for information unavailable to public search.
proposals.model_tier: Browser extraction and rule-based field selection first; a small background model summarizes and prioritizes. Realtime is used only if the owner asks a follow-up by voice.
proposals.latency_budget: Run before the requested delivery time; 1–3 minutes is acceptable. Audio should be ready at the scheduled time, not block a live conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per run: browser actions dominate wall time, while extraction plus a small summary should be a few thousand tokens; avoid sending full page HTML or old history to the model. Audio costs one short synthesis per briefing.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents leave Safari for the local agent/relay and may include sensitive mail or meetings. Store only extracted actionable fields, encrypt job/audio data, and let the owner choose domains and retention. Never send, delete, accept invites, or alter calendar entries automatically; those require explicit confirmation.
missing: A durable scheduled-job runner with per-site extraction recipes
A browser result sanitizer that keeps only requested fields
A small-model summarization/audio pipeline and pendant notification/playback

proposals.user_asks: Open this website, fill out the form with the information we discussed, and show me exactly what is ready before you submit it.
proposals.why_useful: The browser can perform tedious navigation and drafting while preserving the owner's control over irreversible submissions. This is especially useful for support tickets, expense claims, travel forms, and appointment requests behind logins.
proposals.model_tier: Use the planner model to map the request to fields, then deterministic browser actions and a cheap verifier to detect missing/changed values. Realtime only handles conversational clarification.
proposals.latency_budget: Draft in under 30–60 seconds for a normal form; pause immediately when a submit/send/purchase action is reached.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate one-time browser interaction cost; minimize tokens by extracting labels/values and a screenshot only near the final review rather than repeatedly transmitting whole pages.
proposals.security_concerns: A malicious page could alter labels or exfiltrate typed secrets; restrict navigation to the requested origin, redact passwords/one-time codes, and show destination, all field values, attachments, and total cost. Require explicit, fresh confirmation immediately before submit/send/purchase, with an expiry if the page changes.
missing: Origin allowlist and action-risk gate in browser bridge
Structured form-field extraction plus final-page change detection
A review UI that lets the owner approve or edit the exact pending action

proposals.user_asks: Watch this logged-in page and tell me when the status changes, but don't click anything or send anything.
proposals.why_useful: It can monitor order status, application queues, ticket updates, or operational dashboards that are not exposed through public APIs, saving repeated manual checks.
surfaces: Mac Safari browser bridge with browser_wait_for/read
pendant audio alert and dashboard history
proposals.model_tier: Prefer DOM selectors and hashes/rules; use a cheap model only to classify a changed snippet. No realtime model unless the owner asks what the change means.
proposals.latency_budget: Poll at a user-selected interval (for example 15 minutes to 6 hours); alert within one interval. Do not keep a live browser loop when not needed.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low if snapshots are diffed locally and only changed text is summarized; browser polling and wakeups dominate. Retain compact before/after snippets, not full pages.
proposals.security_concerns: Persistent login access and page contents are sensitive. Limit each watch to a declared URL/origin and selector, encrypt state, allow immediate pause/revoke, and prevent all click/type/navigation beyond the watch scope. Alerts may reveal sensitive data aloud, so require a private-mode setting or terse notification.
missing: Persistent watch scheduler with backoff and expiration
Selector/hash diffing and notification deduplication
Per-watch privacy settings and revocation controls

proposals.user_asks: Check my logged-in web accounts for anything urgent, summarize it, and draft (but do not send) any replies that need my attention.
proposals.why_useful: This uses the browser's unique access to authenticated pages, turning scattered inbox/task systems into one concise audio-friendly brief while preserving the owner's control over outbound communication.
surfaces: relay-realtime receives the request and speaks a short confirmation
Mac browser harness opens the relevant existing Safari tabs or navigates to approved services, reads pages, and creates drafts
dashboard and iOS show extracted items, citations, and the exact unsent drafts
pendant plays the finished summary as audio
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background planner/extractor for page parsing and deduplication; use realtime only for the initial conversation and final concise narration. Escalate ambiguous interpretation to the planner model, not the realtime model.
proposals.latency_budget: A 30–90 second background run is acceptable; return partial results service-by-service if one site is slow. Never wait synchronously in a voice turn for the whole sweep.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically low: a few planner calls plus page text tokens; materially cheaper than narrating every page. Audio cost is one short summary, not a continuous browser session.
proposals.security_concerns: Reading private pages is expected, but credentials and page contents must stay on the Mac/relay job scope and not enter durable memory by default. Drafting is reversible; sending mail, posting, or changing account state must stop and display the exact target and content for explicit confirmation.
missing: A first-class authenticated-account sweep job with per-site allowlist and deduplication
A browser result format that preserves URL/title/quoted evidence for citations
A draft artifact state distinct from an executable send action
A background-job-to-audio notification path on the pendant

proposals.user_asks: Every weekday morning, check my logged-in calendar, task board, and travel reservations, then tell me the three things I need to know and prepare a suggested plan.
proposals.why_useful: It provides a personalized morning brief from sources that public search cannot access, without forcing the owner to open multiple services.
surfaces: Mac scheduler runs while the Mac is awake and invokes browser navigation/read actions for the configured services
planner model normalizes events, detects conflicts, and generates a three-item brief
dashboard/iOS show source links and editable plan details
pendant receives a short audio notification and plays it on demand
proposals.model_tier: Scheduled extraction and conflict detection use a cheaper slower model. Realtime only handles follow-up questions when the owner asks about the brief.
proposals.latency_budget: Run 1–3 minutes before the chosen delivery time; tolerate a stale-source warning rather than blocking the entire brief.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate per weekday, dominated by authenticated page extraction and planner context. Cache unchanged pages and send only deltas to keep token cost down; one short audio rendering per brief.
proposals.security_concerns: Store only normalized dates, titles, locations, and links—not full page text or credentials. Travel and calendar data is sensitive; service access should be explicitly configured. Planning is safe, but booking, canceling, or inviting attendees requires confirmation.
missing: Per-routine browser account/service configuration and selectors resilient to UI changes
Delta cache with expiration and source freshness indicators
A durable audio notification/queue for scheduled results
Timezone and sleep/wake handling when the Mac is offline

proposals.user_asks: Watch this logged-in page for a meaningful change and tell me when it happens, with the before-and-after evidence.
proposals.why_useful: It turns browser access into an asynchronous monitor for shipment status, appointments, application portals, price/availability, or account notices without requiring the owner to remember to check.
surfaces: owner creates the monitor from voice or dashboard with URL, cadence, and change description
Mac scheduler runs browser reads on the Safari session and compares normalized page sections
relay stores a compact diff and sends a pendant audio notification plus dashboard evidence
owner can open the cited page and decide whether to act
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic text/DOM hashing and a cheap extraction model for routine diffs; call the planner model only when the change is semantically ambiguous. Realtime is used only for the notification conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: Cadence can be 15 minutes to daily depending on the use case; alert within one polling cycle, not real-time streaming.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low when hashes and targeted selectors avoid full-page model calls; cost scales with polling frequency and page size. Audio is only generated on meaningful changes.
proposals.security_concerns: Repeated private-page access and notifications can reveal sensitive information to anyone near the pendant. Require explicit monitor setup, allow pause/delete, minimize stored snapshots, and never auto-submit or purchase based on a change.
missing: Persistent monitor definitions and per-monitor cadence
Stable selector/region extraction with login/session failure detection
DOM/text diff and sensitive-content redaction
Notification queue with deduplication and quiet hours

proposals.user_asks: Every morning, check my private calendar, travel reservations, and important account notifications in Safari, then give me a concise spoken briefing with links and only flag things that need my attention.
proposals.why_useful: Combines authenticated sources the server cannot access into one hands-free briefing, while avoiding costly realtime browsing during conversation.
proposals.model_tier: Background planner (cheap batch model) runs browser reads and deduplication; realtime model only speaks the final 30–60 second summary. Use server web search only for public context.
proposals.latency_budget: Runs asynchronously in 2–5 minutes; cached result is ready before the owner's routine. Playback starts immediately when requested.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: a handful of browser page extracts plus a short summary; dominant cost is model tokens from changed private pages, reduced by hashes and per-site cursors.
proposals.security_concerns: Private calendar/account content leaves Safari through the local bridge to the Worker. Store only extracted event/task summaries, not page bodies; encrypt in transit/storage. Never click external links that trigger actions; read-only by default and require confirmation for any booking, cancellation, or reply.
missing: Scheduled job trigger with per-site authenticated browser session
Browser extraction normalization and change hashing
Encrypted per-user secret/session policy and retention controls

proposals.user_asks: When I ask, find the exact information on a logged-in website—such as my latest bill, a delivery status, or an insurance claim—and read me the answer, citing the page and date.
proposals.why_useful: Authenticated lookup is the browser tier's unique advantage over public search and avoids making the owner manually hunt through portals.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model classifies intent and confirms the target site; browser agent performs deterministic navigation/extraction; cheap model compresses the result. Escalate to realtime only for ambiguous follow-up conversation.
proposals.latency_budget: First answer in 10–30 seconds; if a site is slow, return a progress notification and finish asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low to moderate per lookup; browser latency dominates, while bounded DOM extraction and a short answer keep token cost small.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not expose full account numbers, health data, or page dumps in audio; redact sensitive fields and speak only requested values. Read-only actions need no confirmation; changing settings, downloading documents, or sending anything requires explicit confirmation.
missing: Site-specific extraction schemas with redaction
Tab/session isolation and sensitive-field redaction before model input
Progress and timeout events surfaced to pendant

proposals.user_asks: Draft a form, email, or support request from information on this private webpage, fill it in, and show me exactly what will be submitted before I approve it.
proposals.why_useful: Turns authenticated browser access into useful work while preserving a hard safety boundary before irreversible external actions.
proposals.model_tier: Background planner extracts facts and drafts with a cheap model; realtime is used only to resolve ambiguities and present the final concise preview.
proposals.latency_budget: Draft within 30–60 seconds. Pause indefinitely at the submit/send button until approval; after approval, a deterministic browser action completes it and returns confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Moderate for long forms; minimize by extracting only relevant labels/values and using local template filling. Browser time and page complexity dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: A malicious page could inject instructions; treat page text as untrusted data and never let it override policy. Display recipient, fields, attachments, amount, and final body. Require explicit one-time confirmation immediately before submit/send/purchase; never reuse approval.
missing: Structured action preview/approval protocol
DOM field mapping with origin and recipient display
Prompt-injection isolation for webpage content

proposals.user_asks: Watch my authenticated order, appointment, and account pages for changes, and tell me only when a meaningful change happens—never pollute my daily briefing with unchanged pages.
