args.change: Add an expiring, tab-bound browser capability lease to the Safari extension protocol. On each heartbeat, Safari issues a random lease ID for the currently attached tab/window; /execute actions must carry that lease and an idempotency key, and results echo the lease plus a DOM-generation counter. Lease rotation on navigation, tab close, or idle timeout makes stale queued clicks and late results harmless without introducing an approval gate. Persist only hashes and audit metadata (not cookies or page contents), and let the Mac planner renew the lease when the owner explicitly asks to continue on the same tab.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Long browser tasks stop acting on the wrong tab after Safari changes pages or the Mac reconnects. The owner can safely say “continue” across multiple agents while private login sessions stay inside Safari, and the action history can explain exactly which tab generation was read or changed.
args.effort: Medium: extension heartbeat/protocol update, browserBridge lease validation, queue schema migration, and tests for navigation, reconnect, duplicate delivery, and two simultaneous tabs.
args.risk: A lease mismatch could abort an otherwise harmless workflow; recover by refreshing the current tab lease and replaying only idempotent reads. Never replay clicks or typing automatically after a generation change. This is observability and stale-command protection, not a user confirmation gate.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few dozen bytes per command/result and a small D1/local metadata record.
args.latency_impact: Under 100 ms for local validation; no extra model round trip. Reconnect may add one heartbeat interval before continuation.
args.security_impact: Improves containment: a stolen or delayed command cannot target a later tab state, and no authentication material leaves Safari. Lease IDs must be high-entropy, short-lived, and excluded from spoken logs.
depends_on: A working durable browser job runner or queue persistence (the current router exists but the durable runner is still open)
Safari extension heartbeat support for tab/window identity and navigation generation
Typed result receipts already present in browserBridge/browserSessions

args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; reduces wasted model and HTTP wait time. Small local JSON/job-state growth for lease and replay metadata.
args.latency_impact: Offline detection becomes heartbeat-lease latency (target 5–10s) rather than 45s; connected reads unchanged.

args.change: Add reconnect-safe command leases and stale-intent quarantine to the Safari bridge. Every queued browser command gets an owner/job id, createdAt, expiresAt, and a lease epoch tied to the extension heartbeat. When a device goes offline, read-only commands may remain resumable, but clicks/types/selects/navigations are quarantined; on reconnect, discard expired or epoch-invalid commands and emit a compact pendant/Mac receipt explaining what was skipped. Mark browser sessions detached when their last heartbeat is stale instead of presenting old tabIds as live. Provide an explicit resume command for a still-valid job rather than silently replaying the backlog.
args.why_useful_to_owner: If Safari drops offline—as it is right now with 7 pending commands—the owner will not later get surprise navigation, typing, or form changes from an old request. They get a clear 'paused/skipped' result and can resume intentional work after reconnect, while safe page reads can continue automatically.
args.effort: Medium: queue schema and worker state machine, heartbeat epoch handling, session staleness projection, receipts, and tests for disconnect/reconnect races.
args.risk: A legitimate long-running read could expire or a reconnect could be misclassified. Recover by retaining quarantined commands for inspection and offering explicit resume; never delete without receipt. No mutation is blocked when intentionally reissued.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local JSON fields and one receipt per expiry/reconnect. No new hardware.
args.latency_impact: No added latency while online; reconnect performs one reconciliation pass before accepting new commands.
args.security_impact: Improves safety against replay into an authenticated session. Keep URLs, extracted text, and mutation payloads out of generic heartbeat logs; store them only in the job's protected receipt.

args.user_asks: “If a logged-in website signs me out while you’re working, tell me immediately, pause safely, and let me resume the unfinished task after I sign back in.”
args.why_useful: Authenticated browser work currently has stale sessions and the extension can disappear; without auth-state awareness, a workflow may fail ambiguously or leave a filled draft in an unknown state. This gives the owner a precise, spoken recovery path without exposing credentials or replaying actions into the wrong account.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background classifier for page/auth-state detection and receipt generation; reserve realtime only for the pendant alert and the owner's follow-up conversation.
args.latency_budget: Detect on each browser result (under 200 ms locally) and deliver the pendant notification on the next relay poll/stream (typically under 2 s). Resume validation can take one browser round trip.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental model cost for URL/status heuristics; occasional small classifier call only for ambiguous login pages. Dominant cost is one browser snapshot when a result indicates redirect or auth error.
args.security_concerns: Never inspect, store, or transmit passwords, OTPs, cookies, or page form values from credential fields. Store only origin, account label if already known, auth-state reason, tab/session fingerprint, and a redacted draft receipt. Require the owner to perform reauthentication directly in Safari; resume must revalidate origin and tab before any action.
missing: A browser auth-state detector recognizing login redirects, 401/403 pages, consent screens, and expired-session interstitials without reading secrets
A durable paused-job record that stores the next safe step and redacted draft state
A reconnect/resume handshake between the Safari extension and relay, including a user-visible 'reauthenticated' signal
A pendant notification/event type for browser authentication loss

args.change: Implement an authenticated-session sentinel between browser results and job receipts. For every browser result, classify only navigation metadata/status/title and non-sensitive DOM markers for signed-out states (login redirect, 401/403, expired-session interstitial, consent wall). On detection, atomically pause the job at the next action, emit a redacted auth_lost event to the relay, and persist a resumable checkpoint. After the extension reports the same origin and a fresh tab fingerprint, require a new browser_snapshot and mark the checkpoint revalidated before continuing; never replay the pre-auth action automatically.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A private-site task stops clearly at the moment Safari logs out instead of failing mysteriously or continuing against a login page. The pendant says which site needs attention, and after the owner signs in they can continue without losing the prepared, unsent work.
args.effort: Medium: detector rules plus a small site-agnostic marker schema, atomic job pause/checkpoint state, relay event plumbing, and resume tests across redirects and tab replacement.
args.risk: Some sites use unusual login pages and may cause false pauses; recovery is an explicit 'resume after snapshot' action and a per-origin rule override. False negatives are limited by refusing to continue when the expected page role does not match the checkpoint.
args.cost_impact: Minimal storage and relay traffic; mostly local metadata. One extra snapshot on reauthentication; no continuous model call required.
args.latency_impact: Sub-200 ms metadata check per browser result; one extra browser round trip only when resuming.
args.security_impact: Reduces credential/session confusion. Credentials, cookies, OTPs, and input values remain inside Safari; logs contain only origin, redacted reason, and fingerprints.

args.security_concerns: Keep raw private page text on the Mac where possible; send the relay only redacted fields, source URLs, timestamps, and short evidence snippets. Enforce origin/session binding so data from unrelated accounts cannot be silently joined. Never infer or display credentials, tokens, or sensitive form fields unless explicitly requested.

args.change: Add a privacy-scoped cross-origin fact joiner for browser research. The joiner must reject implicit joins across origins, expire its scratch facts after the job, and hand only the redacted discrepancy graph to relay speech and the review-only planner.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask whether two private systems agree and get an answer they can verify, without dumping whole logged-in pages into cloud context or risking an accidental edit. This turns fragmented private browser access into a trustworthy reconciliation tool.
args.effort: Medium-high: typed extraction contracts, local normalization and entity matching, provenance graph, sensitivity-aware projection, and integration tests for mismatched reservations/invoices/calendar entries.
args.risk: Ambiguous matches could produce a false discrepancy or miss one. Show candidate matches and confidence, retain source citations locally for review, and never create an action plan when identity confidence is below threshold.
args.cost_impact: Small local storage footprint; model cost is limited to normalization and ambiguous matching. Cloud payloads are smaller because only typed facts and evidence hashes leave the Mac.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 2–8 seconds for parallel extraction and comparison; no mutation latency because this is review-only.

args.latency_budget: Read the active page and return a proposed event in under 8 seconds; calendar/reminder creation in under 5 seconds after the owner says save. If the browser or Mac is offline, retain the extracted candidate and resume rather than silently dropping it.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one small background extraction call plus one short realtime turn; typically <$0.01 per invocation, dominated by page-text tokens. Avoid sending unrelated page content by extracting only date-bearing regions and a short citation.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page text may contain private order or health information; keep extraction and citations local to the Mac/relay, redact unrelated text, and show the exact title/date/time/timezone/location before writing. Creating a reminder is reversible, but never submit forms or send messages as part of this workflow.

Round 89 findings:

- The browser enqueue grants are still schemas only; every wrapper returns an implementation error.
- A direct `POST /execute` browser navigation timed out.
- Safari is currently offline. The only reported device is stale `home-chrome`; it has no tab, while the bridge reports **8 pending commands**.
- Existing browser sessions are stale records and do not represent usable live tabs.
- I notified `mac-planner` not to assume authenticated browser access.

What I still need:

1. A functioning browser-command enqueue implementation, or an operational extension poll/result path.
2. Safari to heartbeat with a live tab before authenticated page work can be performed.
3. The pending-command queue to be reconciled or purged; otherwise old commands could execute unexpectedly after reconnect.
4. The previously requested owner workflow/sensitivity context remains unavailable; I will work with the existing policy in the meantime.

I recorded two proposals: an authenticated-page-to-calendar workflow and browser command leases/reconnect quarantine to prevent stale actions from replaying.

args.change: Build a local, policy-driven page-minimization layer in the Safari extension. Before authenticated page content leaves the browser, the extension should extract only the requested semantic fields (for example: dates, sender, subject, amount, status, or visible form labels), redact passwords, payment details, tokens, health identifiers, and unrelated DOM regions, and attach the source URL plus a short DOM citation. The relay/model receives the minimized typed payload rather than an entire page dump. If extraction confidence is low, return a redacted preview and ask the owner to name the needed field instead of escalating to full-page transfer. Maintain an owner-visible audit record of what fields crossed the boundary.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Today the owner cannot safely use the browser tier for many authenticated pages: answering a simple question may transmit an entire private page, including secrets or unrelated personal data. This would let them use the pendant to get precise answers from logged-in sites while keeping most of the page inside Safari, without adding an approval gate to ordinary actions.
args.effort: High: extension-side DOM semantic extraction and redaction rules, a typed request contract from the planner, per-origin rule storage, citation generation, and end-to-end tests across dynamic pages and iframes. Requires changing the extension protocol and the browser bridge, not merely prompt instructions.
args.risk: A redaction rule can hide a field or misclassify sensitive text; fail closed for unknown sensitive-looking regions, expose extraction confidence, and permit an explicit owner-selected field expansion. Dynamic sites may defeat selectors; fall back to accessibility-tree fields and retain only the minimum requested region. Recovery is a clearly labeled local preview, never silent full-page upload.
args.cost_impact: Small additional extension CPU and storage cost; lower model/API cost because fewer tokens leave the browser. No hardware cost. Rule updates and audits require engineering and maintenance.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local extraction on ordinary pages; it should reduce model latency substantially by shrinking context. Complex pages may take a few seconds and should report progress.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves privacy by enforcing data minimization before the relay/model boundary. Keep credentials and raw DOM local; encrypt and rotate the field-level audit log; never include redacted values in diagnostics or failure traces.
depends_on: A real browser enqueue implementation and extension protocol capable of typed extraction requests/results
A planner contract that declares the minimum fields needed for each browser question
Extension-side secure storage for per-origin redaction/extraction policies
A relay-side schema validator that rejects unexpected fields

transcript.text:
Recorded a new browser-harness change: **privacy-preserving authenticated-page assistance**.

The owner should be able to ask the pendant precise questions about logged-in pages without sending the entire page to the model. The Safari extension would locally extract only the requested fields, redact credentials and unrelated sensitive data, attach a minimal citation, and send only that typed result onward.

It requires:

- A working browser enqueue/extension protocol
- Typed field requests from the planner
- Extension-side DOM/accessibility extraction and redaction
- Per-origin secure policies and audit records
- Relay-side schema validation rejecting unexpected fields

This is not an approval gate; ordinary actions remain available, but private page content is minimized before it leaves Safari.

args.user_asks: When I’m looking at a private webpage, let me ask about it from the pendant and get a concise, sourced answer; keep the answer tied to that tab, and let me say “prepare that” to fill the reversible parts without sending or submitting anything.
args.why_useful: This combines the browser’s unique access to logged-in pages with the pendant’s hands-free voice and the Mac/relay’s ability to retain a short-lived task context. The owner can leave the desk, ask about the exact page they were viewing, and receive evidence rather than a generic web answer. It also turns a one-shot extraction into a safe reviewable workflow.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the short spoken question and answer; background/cheaper model for extraction normalization and drafting. Escalate to the expensive tier only when the page is ambiguous or the owner asks for synthesis across tabs.
args.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds for an already-captured page context; up to 15 seconds for a fresh read of one tab. Draft/fill may take 10–30 seconds and must stop before submit/send.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per interaction depending on page length and whether synthesis is needed; browser round trips and context tokens dominate, not the small metadata operations.
args.security_concerns: Private DOM text must stay in the authenticated browser-to-local-agent path and only the minimum cited snippets should be sent to the model/relay. Bind context to tabId/session and expire it after roughly 15 minutes or navigation. Never speak secrets by default; redact credentials and payment data. Filling is reversible, but submission, sending, purchasing, or account changes remain an explicit final step the system does not perform.
missing: A live Safari heartbeat and functioning browser command enqueue path; current status is offline and POST /execute browser navigation times out.
A short-lived page-context record containing tab/session identity, extracted snippets, source URL, timestamp, and redaction metadata, addressable from the voice turn.
A pendant-to-browser continuation intent that resolves pronouns such as “that” against the active page context and produces a reviewable fill plan.

args.change: Add a browser-bridge liveness and recovery controller: commands are leased to a device only while its heartbeat is fresh; stale claims automatically return to a pending queue, device selection prefers the real Safari registration, and an offline result is surfaced immediately instead of waiting 45 seconds. Add a startup probe that can bootstrap a tab with browser_navigate once Safari returns, plus an operator-visible count of orphaned commands.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Private-page requests will either work promptly or clearly tell the owner that Safari is unavailable. A sleeping/restarted extension will no longer strand work against the dead home-chrome registration or make the pendant appear frozen.
args.effort: Moderate: bridge queue state machine, heartbeat freshness/lease expiry, deterministic device selection, and tests for restart/race conditions.
args.risk: A command could be reclaimed while Safari is still executing, causing duplicate navigation or extraction. Use command IDs/idempotency keys and mark late results as duplicates; never replay mutations automatically. Recovery is deleting/retrying the orphaned command.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small durable queue/heartbeat metadata. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Offline detection in under a heartbeat interval rather than a 45-second timeout; online actions unchanged, with at most one retry for a read-only command.
args.security_impact: Improves isolation by preventing commands from being delivered to the wrong registered browser. Device identity and tab/session affinity must be enforced; do not auto-replay irreversible browser actions.
depends_on: A functioning Safari extension heartbeat and browser command enqueue implementation
Existing /browser/poll and /browser/result/:commandId semantics
Existing browser session/tab affinity and action receipts

args.user_asks: Before I submit a form on a private site, compare its important fields with the matching information in my other logged-in accounts and documents, point out any conflicts with cited evidence, and prepare corrections without submitting anything.
args.why_useful: People routinely encounter stale addresses, mismatched names, duplicate account numbers, and conflicting dates across portals. Today the browser can inspect a page or fill a form, but it cannot act as a cross-account consistency checker that explains which value differs, where each value came from, and what correction would be made. This prevents expensive mistakes while keeping the owner in control of the final submission.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for field extraction, normalization, and deterministic comparisons; use realtime only to answer the owner's spoken questions or summarize conflicts. Escalate to the expensive tier only for genuinely ambiguous identity/entity matching.
args.latency_budget: 15–30 seconds to inspect the active form and up to three explicitly selected authenticated sources; under 3 seconds for a spoken explanation once the comparison packet exists.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.12 per check; browser extraction and transmitting several source snippets dominate. Deterministic field comparisons should avoid repeated model calls.
args.security_concerns: Only inspect tabs/accounts the owner explicitly names or has selected; never search arbitrary private tabs. Keep raw values local where possible, send normalized fields plus minimal evidence, redact credentials and financial secrets, and expire comparison packets quickly. Do not change any field or submit automatically. The owner must review the proposed before/after values.
missing: A multi-tab authenticated comparison packet with field-level provenance, normalization rules, and confidence scores.
A browser-side field mapper that can identify semantic form fields and corresponding source fields across heterogeneous logged-in sites.
A pendant/Mac review surface that presents conflicts compactly and accepts per-field keep/correct decisions before invoking reversible fill actions.

args.model_tier: Realtime model handles the short spoken pause/resume interaction; a cheaper background worker classifies queued browser steps, expires unsafe work, and produces the audit summary.
args.latency_budget: Pause must reach the Mac/browser within 2 seconds of a pendant departure event; resume status within 5 seconds of return. No model call is needed for the hot-path freeze.

args.user_asks: “Warn me through the pendant if a page I open looks like a fake login or payment page, and tell me the safe official site to use instead.”
args.why_useful: The browser is the only surface that can see the owner’s existing session, page origin, redirects, certificate-facing metadata, and rendered login/payment form. A Mac-local detector can catch lookalike domains, suspicious redirects, injected fields, and brand mismatches before credentials or card data are entered; the relay can interrupt the pendant even when the owner is away from the Mac. Today the owner has no cross-surface warning that combines the actual page with an immediate spoken alternative.
args.model_tier: Run a small local/cheap classifier first using URL, origin, redirect chain, DOM labels, and visual branding. Use the expensive realtime model only if signals conflict and the owner asks a spoken follow-up; never upload passwords, form values, cookies, or page screenshots by default.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms for deterministic domain/redirect checks and under 3 seconds for local visual/DOM analysis; the pendant warning should arrive before the owner submits or types into a newly detected credential form.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for allowlists, URL reputation, and local heuristics; roughly $0.001–$0.01 for an ambiguous local-model classification. Realtime cost occurs only on explicit follow-up.
args.security_concerns: This must be detection-only: no automatic credential handling, form submission, or navigation to a replacement site. Keep sensitive page data on the Mac; transmit only risk category, domain, confidence, and a safe destination candidate. False positives must be dismissible, and the detector must never claim a page is safe—only that it found no known warning signs.
missing: A browser-extension event stream for navigation, redirect, form-focus, and submit-intent events rather than command polling alone
A signed, locally cached registry of the owner’s known official domains and preferred recovery links
A Mac-local URL/DOM/visual phishing detector with explainable signals and a strict no-secret-data input contract
A low-latency relay interrupt that can deliver a security warning to the pendant and accept “dismiss” or “read reasons”
A browser-side pre-submit observation hook that can warn without blocking or requiring a confirmation gate

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **real-time phishing and payment-page warnings through the pendant**.

The owner should be warned when a newly opened page resembles a fake login or payment site, with an explanation and the official destination suggested. Delivering it requires browser navigation/form-focus events, a local URL/DOM/visual detector, an official-domain registry, and a low-latency relay interrupt—without collecting secrets or blocking actions.

args.user_asks: “Compare the information across my logged-in sites and Mac, tell me what conflicts or changed, and prepare the next steps without sending or submitting anything.”
args.why_useful: This is a genuinely cross-surface task: Safari can read private portals that the Mac APIs cannot, while the Mac can read local Calendar/Mail and create a review artifact. The owner gets one evidence-backed answer instead of manually reconciling tabs and local data.
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for multi-page extraction, normalization, and conflict detection; use realtime only to clarify the owner's target entities and speak the final concise result. Use the local Mac model for deterministic file/calendar assembly.
args.latency_budget: A voice acknowledgement in under 2 seconds; background reconciliation in 1–3 minutes depending on authenticated tabs. Never wait on a single browser poll in the realtime turn; report completion through the pendant and dashboard.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly 1 background model call per source batch plus one reconciliation call (dominant cost is DOM extraction/context resend); realtime cost is limited to acknowledgement and final summary. Local Mac actions add no model API cost.
args.security_concerns: Private page text and local calendar facts leave Safari/Mac only to the relay/model for this explicit request. Store source URLs, timestamps, and short evidence hashes rather than raw page bodies by default; redact secrets and tokens. Filling drafts is allowed, but sending/submitting/purchasing remains outside the workflow and must never occur implicitly.
missing: A first-class cross-source entity/field normalizer and conflict report (not merely a page watch)
A durable job that can resume when Safari is offline and preserve per-source evidence across browser polls
A review artifact linking each conclusion to its Safari URL/DOM snippet and Mac source, with expiration when either source becomes stale
A working browser command enqueue implementation; the currently granted enqueue tools are schemas/stubs and Safari is presently offline with pending commands

args.user_asks: “If one of my logged-in sites signs out or asks for verification while you’re working, tell me immediately, pause that site, and continue the parts you safely can.”
args.why_useful: Browser automation currently risks treating a login page, MFA challenge, CAPTCHA, or expired session as ordinary content. Detecting auth-state transitions lets the owner recover the session without losing a multi-site job, while independent Mac/local work can continue and the pendant can warn them promptly.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic browser heuristics and a cheap classifier for auth/MFA/CAPTCHA detection; use realtime only for the short spoken alert and any owner clarification. Do not spend the expensive model on every poll.
args.latency_budget: Detect on every browser result (sub-second locally), alert within 5 seconds of the extension result, and checkpoint/resume the remaining job asynchronously. No repeated polling while the site is blocked.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for URL/title/DOM heuristics; occasional small classifier call only for ambiguous pages. Main cost is durable checkpoint storage and one resumed extraction call.
args.security_concerns: Never extract or transmit OTP values, passwords, recovery codes, or CAPTCHA contents. Store only the blocked origin, reason category, timestamp, and the last safe checkpoint. Resuming after re-authentication should require an explicit owner signal (e.g. “continue”), but unrelated reversible local steps may proceed.
missing: A browser result schema with an auth-state classification and safe redacted metadata
Durable per-step checkpoint/skip semantics in the browser job runner
A pendant notification event and dashboard queue item for blocked browser jobs
A tested recovery path when Safari reconnects after offline periods

args.user_asks: “Use my logged-in websites to answer this, but keep the private page contents on my devices—send only the specific fields needed for the answer, and show me exactly what left each device.”
args.why_useful: Today the browser can reach sessions that other nodes cannot, but a useful answer may require sending broad page text into a model context. This gives the owner practical data minimization: Safari extracts only an approved schema, the Mac performs joins or calculations locally where possible, and the pendant reports the sources and fields disclosed.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic local extraction and Mac-side computation first. Use a small background model only to map page labels to the owner's requested fields; use realtime only to explain the disclosure receipt or resolve an ambiguous field.
args.latency_budget: Preview the disclosure manifest within 2 seconds, extract and compute in under 30 seconds for ordinary pages, and ask no follow-up unless a requested field is ambiguous or unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost: most work is browser DOM selection and local computation. A small model call is needed only for semantic field mapping; raw page bodies are not sent, reducing context and token cost.
args.security_concerns: Selectors and field values can themselves be sensitive, so redact values in logs and retain only field names, origin, timestamp, and hashes by default. The owner must be able to inspect the exact outbound field manifest before execution. Never extract passwords, OTPs, recovery codes, or payment secrets. A deliberate override may permit a raw snippet for a single field, with an expiring receipt.
missing: A declarative per-request data-minimization manifest and field allowlist
A Safari-side extraction operation that returns typed fields without returning the full page
A Mac-local computation/merge endpoint that accepts typed browser fields and produces a result
A disclosure receipt visible on the pendant and dashboard, with retention and deletion controls

args.user_asks: “When you tell me something from a logged-in site, prove that it was observed live just now, identify the exact account and tab it came from, and warn me if the evidence is stale or ambiguous.”
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently distinguish a live authenticated observation from a cached session, an old browser result, or a page that silently redirected to login. A compact freshness and provenance proof makes private-browser answers trustworthy without exposing the whole page.
args.model_tier: Generate provenance deterministically from the extension result (tab/session, URL, title, observed timestamp, DOM-region hash, redirect/auth state). Use a cheaper model only to summarize the cited evidence; realtime speaks the short verdict.
args.latency_budget: Attach the proof during the same browser round trip; under 5 seconds for a normal read. Refuse to present a definitive answer when the tab heartbeat or evidence age exceeds the request's freshness bound.
args.cost_estimate: Very low API cost: hashing and timestamp validation are local. Only the final natural-language summary uses a model, with short cited snippets rather than full page context.
args.security_concerns: Do not reveal account identifiers beyond a user-chosen friendly label; hash or redact URLs containing tokens and query parameters. Keep DOM hashes and evidence snippets short-lived and deletable. The proof must attest to observation metadata, not claim that a page's content is truthful.
missing: A typed browser observation receipt with tab/session identity, redirect chain, observation time, freshness deadline, and DOM-region hash
Clock/heartbeat validation between Safari and the Mac agent
A user-visible citation card and pendant speech format for freshness, account label, and ambiguity
A policy that prevents stale observations from being silently reused as current answers

args.change: Introduce a privacy-preserving browser observation protocol: Safari returns typed, owner-approved fields plus a signed observation receipt (device/session, tab, origin, timestamp, redirect/auth state, freshness deadline, and region hashes), while raw DOM remains on the Mac. The Mac performs joins and calculations locally and sends the relay only the minimal result and citation metadata. Expired receipts become unusable rather than silently falling back to cached text.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask questions about private sites without making entire pages part of model context, while hearing whether each answer is live, which session produced it, and exactly what was disclosed.
args.effort: High: extension extraction contract, local field mapper, receipt signing/verification, Mac-local computation service, disclosure UI, and compatibility fallback for pages that cannot expose typed fields.
args.risk: Some sites will resist stable selectors or change layout; fall back to an explicit ambiguous/unavailable result, never broad extraction by default. Clock skew or an extension restart could invalidate receipts; recover by reacquiring the page and issuing a new receipt.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and hashing overhead; reduced model-token cost because raw pages are withheld. Engineering cost is substantial across extension, Mac bridge, and dashboard.
args.latency_impact: One extra local validation step, typically tens of milliseconds; complex field mapping may add seconds but avoids transmitting and summarizing full pages.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces sensitive data exposure and makes stale/cross-account evidence detectable. Signing keys must remain in the extension/Mac secure store; receipts should not contain secrets or full URLs with query tokens.
depends_on: A browser extension result schema that supports typed fields and redacted metadata
Mac-local field computation and receipt verification
Owner-facing disclosure and freshness UI/audio

transcript.text:
Recorded three new items:

- **Minimal-field private browsing:** use authenticated sites while keeping raw page contents on-device; send only owner-approved fields.
- **Live provenance proofs:** every browser-derived answer carries freshness, tab/session, account label, redirect state, and evidence metadata.
- **Privacy-preserving observation protocol:** Safari emits typed fields plus signed receipts; the Mac performs local joins/calculations, and stale receipts cannot be silently reused.

These require new typed browser-result contracts, local Mac-side computation and receipt verification, disclosure/freshness UI, and a functioning browser enqueue path.

args.change: Add a local, declarative cross-tab comparison primitive that accepts two tab leases plus a field-extraction/redaction schema, computes normalized differences on the Mac, and emits only a typed discrepancy packet (field, values, source locator, confidence, timestamp). The raw DOM never enters the relay prompt; the packet is encrypted, short-lived, and invalidated if either tab navigates.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can catch billing, booking, policy, or account inconsistencies across private sites without handing complete sensitive pages to the cloud or manually copying them between tabs.
args.effort: High: extension must read two leased tabs, Mac bridge needs a local extraction/normalization engine and schema validation, and relay/pendant need discrepancy-packet rendering with citations.
args.risk: Incorrect selectors or normalization could produce a false mismatch or miss one; show source fields and confidence and label the result as a comparison aid, never an authoritative financial or medical decision. No write action is permitted.
args.cost_impact: Small local CPU/storage cost; lower recurring model cost because only normalized fields and mismatches are sent, typically a few kilobytes.
args.latency_impact: Adds local extraction time (roughly seconds) but avoids full-page upload and reduces remote context latency.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces data exfiltration and retention, but the local Mac process still handles sensitive data; enforce per-tab leases, encrypted temporary files, TTL deletion, and audit records.

args.user_asks: “If Safari is unavailable, remember the private-page task and resume it when my browser reconnects—tell me if anything changed, and never run the same step twice.”
args.why_useful: Today a private browser request can sit in nine stale commands or consume a 45-second timeout, then fail with no reliable handoff. This would let the owner leave the Mac or close Safari without losing the request, while preserving authenticated-page access that the relay cannot provide. It would resume only the unfinished read/extract work, report the exact last completed step, and avoid duplicate navigation or mutations.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for queue bookkeeping, retry classification, and change comparison; use realtime only to acknowledge the owner's request and speak the final concise update. Browser extraction can invoke the stronger model only when page structure or semantic change is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 2 seconds; detect bridge absence within 10 seconds instead of waiting 45 seconds; resume within one polling interval (up to 30 seconds) after Safari heartbeat. No repeated 45-second blocking waits.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per resumed read, dominated by page extraction and semantic diff; heartbeat/lease bookkeeping is negligible. No relay Browser Run spend for owner-private pages.
args.security_concerns: Private URLs and extracted text remain on the owner's Mac/relay path and must not be failed over to public Browser Run. Persist only encrypted job metadata and evidence hashes by default, with short-lived page text. Read-only steps may resume automatically; if the task reaches typing, sending, submitting, or purchasing, stop and present the exact pending action rather than replaying it. Every step needs an idempotency key and tab/session binding.
missing: A device heartbeat lease with explicit device identity and reconnect generation; Safari currently disappears from /browser/status while nine commands remain pending.
A circuit breaker that marks queued commands stale after lease expiry, quarantines them, and emits a reconnectable job rather than allowing blind 45-second waits.
Durable per-step checkpoint storage and replay classification (completed, safely retryable, or requires owner review), plus a single result stream to the pendant and dashboard.
A Mac-side reconnect hint/health action so the owner can be told Safari is not polling without treating home-chrome as a substitute.

args.change: Implement a browser-bridge lease/circuit-breaker between /browser/status, /execute, and the existing command queue. Assign each extension installation a reconnect generation and heartbeat lease; when the lease expires, atomically quarantine all pending commands for that device, cancel their 45-second waiters, and materialize a durable job checkpoint (step id, idempotency key, tab/session binding, evidence, and safe-retry classification). On a newer heartbeat, offer/resume only checkpoints whose generation and tab affinity still match; mark old-generation click/type steps stale instead of replaying them. Emit one reconnect-needed event to the Mac planner, pendant relay, and dashboard, with queue age and exact recovery instruction. This is deliberately narrower than the proposed durable runner: it prevents stale-command execution and makes the current queue truthful even before full job persistence exists.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops seeing misleading 45-second browser failures and stops risking duplicate actions after Safari returns. They get one clear message such as “Safari bridge is not polling; 9 commands paused,” and private read tasks continue from the last verified page step when the same session returns.
args.effort: Medium: bridge state machine and atomic queue transitions, a small durable checkpoint store, reconnect event wiring, and tests for crash/reconnect/generation mismatch. No new browser extension UI is required beyond heartbeat payload fields.
args.risk: A false lease expiry could pause harmless work; recover by retaining quarantined commands and allowing explicit retry. A Safari restart may invalidate tab IDs, so read-only navigation can be replanned while click/type actions remain stale. Never delete commands silently; expose quarantine and replay receipts.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly one small D1/local JSON checkpoint per command and heartbeat metadata. Avoids wasting relay browser minutes and repeated model retries.
args.latency_impact: Health failure detected in 10–15 seconds; removes the current 45-second blocking wait. Reconnect resumes on the next heartbeat, typically under 30 seconds.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by binding replay to extension generation, device, tab, and session; reduces chance of replaying a stale authenticated mutation. Checkpoint evidence should be minimized/short-retained and page text never sent to the public browser backend.
depends_on: Expose a stable Safari extensionId/device lease and reconnect generation in heartbeat/status.
Reuse existing idempotency keys and receipts from browserBridge/browserSessions rather than creating a second action identity.
Add a small event consumer in mac-planner/relay for reconnect-needed and resumed-job updates.

transcript.text:
Round 95 findings:

- `/browser/status` currently reports **offline**, with only the unused `home-chrome` device and **9 pending commands**. Safari is absent.
- `/browser/inspections` is empty.
- Recent browser jobs failed after the full **45-second timeout**, confirming the queue still waits blindly when the bridge disappears.
- I recorded this as an active stale-queue/device-identity defect and notified `mac-planner`.

I proposed two related pieces:

1. **Owner capability:** pause private-page work safely when Safari disappears, preserve the exact checkpoint, and resume only compatible read steps when the same browser session reconnects.
2. **Browser-harness change:** add heartbeat leases, reconnect generations, an atomic circuit breaker, stale-command quarantine, idempotent checkpoints, and reconnect events for the pendant, relay, Mac planner, and dashboard.

What I still need is implementation—not another discovery call:

- A functioning live browser command enqueue path; the granted enqueue tools remain stubs.
- Safari heartbeat/device identity and reconnect-generation fields.
- Queue logic that cancels the current 45-second waiter and persists quarantine/checkpoint state.
- A reconnect event consumer in the planner/relay so the owner receives one actionable status update rather than repeated failures.

The largest unknown is whether Safari is merely closed/disabled or whether the extension’s heartbeat path itself is broken; the current API cannot distinguish those states.

args.user_asks: “While I’m looking at a private webpage, let me ask the pendant questions about this exact tab; keep the context only while I’m there, and forget it when I leave.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner must explicitly initiate a browser extraction and cannot have a natural, hands-free conversation anchored to the page already in front of them. This would make the pendant a private-page companion: they could ask “what does this fee mean?”, “which date is listed?”, or “compare these two visible options” without copying URLs or exposing the page to a general web search. The context would be intentionally ephemeral rather than becoming long-term memory.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the short spoken question and turn-taking; a cheaper background model prepares a compact page capsule and extracts cited regions. Escalate to the stronger model only for multi-section comparison or ambiguous page structure.
args.latency_budget: Active-tab context should be available within 1 second of a tab-focus/page-change event; spoken answers within 3 seconds for visible text. A tab transition should revoke the capsule immediately, with no background polling after revocation.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.003–$0.02 per question, dominated by sending the selected page region and generating the answer; tab-focus events and capsule revocation are negligible. No public-browser fallback should be used for authenticated content.
args.security_concerns: Page text stays in a short-lived, encrypted context capsule scoped to extension installation, window, tab, and navigation generation. Do not retain passwords, payment fields, hidden DOM, or unrelated tabs; redact likely secrets before model submission. Destroy the capsule on navigation, tab close, explicit “forget,” or a short idle TTL. Answers must cite the visible region and say when the page is no longer available. This is read-only and must never infer permission to click, type, send, or submit.
missing: A browser extension event stream for active-tab focus, navigation generation, close, and visible-region changes; polling command results alone cannot establish when context should be revoked.
A server-side ephemeral page capsule store with strict tab/navigation scoping, redaction, TTL, and an explicit destruction acknowledgement.
A low-latency route that joins pendant voice turns to the current browser capsule without placing the full page into every model prompt.
A compact spoken citation format and dashboard transcript showing which tab and page region supported each answer.

args.user_asks: “When I double-tap the pendant while text is selected in Safari, save that exact quote with its page title, URL, timestamp, and a short spoken label into a notebook on my Mac.”
args.why_useful: The owner can currently read a private page, but capturing reliable evidence means manually switching apps, copying text, and recording where it came from. This creates a one-gesture, authenticated-page citation capture useful for research, receipts, policies, and work discussions. It is not a page watch or a drafted transaction: it captures only the owner-selected excerpt, preserving the source while avoiding a copy of the whole private page.
args.model_tier: No expensive realtime reasoning is needed for capture. Firmware sends the gesture; the browser bridge reads the selected range; a cheap model optionally generates a short label only when requested. Realtime can confirm capture with a brief spoken response.
args.latency_budget: Gesture acknowledgement under 300 ms locally; selected text and metadata saved within 2 seconds. If Safari is unavailable, the pendant stores a tiny pending capture intent and confirms that no quote was taken rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.002 per capture, with almost no model cost unless auto-labeling is enabled. Storage is small: quote, source metadata, hash, and optional label.
args.security_concerns: Only the browser's explicit current selection is transferred; never scrape the rest of the DOM or neighboring tabs. Redact password/payment-like selections and require a second deliberate gesture for unusually long excerpts. Store the citation in the owner's local Mac notebook by default, with encrypted relay transport and a configurable retention period. The result must include a content hash so later edits are detectable.
missing: A browser extension command/event that returns the current selection plus canonical URL, title, tab ID, and navigation generation.
A pendant double-tap gesture event routed to the active browser session, with local debounce and offline intent buffering.
A Mac notebook destination with append-only citation records and a stable schema for quote, source, timestamp, hash, and label.
A receipt linking the physical gesture, selected range, browser tab, and saved file so the owner can audit or delete a capture.

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **Ephemeral “talk to this page” mode**  
   Ask the pendant questions about the exact private Safari tab currently open, with tab-scoped context that is destroyed on navigation, tab close, explicit forget, or TTL expiry.

2. **One-gesture citation capture**  
   Double-tap the pendant to save only the selected Safari text with its title, URL, timestamp, navigation generation, and content hash into a Mac notebook.

Both require new wiring rather than merely exposing existing routes:

- Safari active-tab, selection, navigation, and close events.
- Strict tab/navigation-scoped ephemeral context capsules.
- Pendant gesture routing and local debounce/buffering.
- A local citation notebook schema and auditable receipts.
- Secret redaction and deletion/retention controls.

result.summary: Add a durable browser job runner with two backends: the authenticated Safari bridge for owner-private pages and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages. Represent each step as navigate/read/extract/click/type, persist evidence (URL, title, timestamp, selected text), retry transient failures, and expose a job result stream to the planner.
result.note: KEPT OPEN: the backend ROUTER now exists, the durable job runner still does not. Backend A ships: local-agent/browserSessions.js (chg-bc35ae04 / chg-2fffc681 / chg-086a6904). Backend B ships: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js (chg-81e5c92d, implemented). ROUTER DONE 2026-08-07 — local-agent/originFanOut.js chooseBackend() is the selector this entry named: owner-private -> Safari (only it holds the sessions); public -> Browser Run (only it is awake when the Mac sleeps); LAN / private IP / localhost -> Safari only, decided by serverBrowser.normalizePublicUrl rather than a second copy of that logic; relay budget spent -> Safari; explicit backend:"safari"|"relay" always honoured. An owner-private page is deliberately NOT failed over to the relay when Safari is down: the relay cannot hold the session, so the trip buys a login wall at the price of one of ten daily browser-minutes, and reserving that budget is what keeps the public leg answerable. Free-tier limits are enforced rather than documented: relay lane is serial, paced to 1 action per 10s, and a UTC-day browser-ms tally persists in .pendant-relay-browser-budget.json (GET /origins/budget). MISSING STILL: no durable job runner — no jobId, no persistence across a restart, no retry of transient failures — and no job result stream to the planner. serverBrowser is still unreachable from the voice path (chg-f527c3bc, unapplied wiring diff).

Replace the current single 45-second wait with progress events and resumable polling.
result.note: KEPT OPEN deliberately for one verified, still-true defect. Covered: request ids, tab/session affinity and typed results by local-agent/browserBridge.js + browserSessions.js (chg-bc35ae04 / chg-086a6904); idempotency keys now exist per action as content-addressed ids and are surfaced at GET /journal (chg-aace6694). NOT done, verified in the current source: local-agent/browserBridge.js:123 waitForBrowserResult(commandId, timeoutMs = 45_000) is still a single 45-second blocking wait, with COMMAND_LEASE_MS = 45_000 at browserBridge.js:5 — no progress events, no resumable polling. The "explicit irreversible-action checkpoints" clause is refused rather than pending: owner policy is no approval gates.

args.evidence: GET /browser/status and GET /browser/poll responses in this round

args.user_asks: “If you lose my Safari connection halfway through a browser task, pause safely, remember exactly where you were, and continue when Safari returns—without repeating clicks or losing the private-page evidence; tell me if anything needs my attention.”
args.why_useful: Today an authenticated workflow can sit in a 45-second wait while a stale or wrong device repeatedly claims it; reconnecting risks duplicate navigation/clicks or forces the owner to start over. A fenced, resumable workflow gives the owner reliable continuity across the only browser that holds their logins, the Mac planner, the always-awake relay, and the pendant notification path.
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model runs checkpoint reconciliation, stale-command classification, and evidence diffing; realtime is used only for a short pendant alert when a workflow pauses or resumes.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint each browser action in under 1 second; detect a dead lease within 30–60 seconds; resume within 10 seconds of a verified Safari heartbeat. No owner wait for the background reconciliation.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per reconnect depending on page-text reconciliation; most runs are metadata/hash comparisons and use no expensive model. Voice alert cost is negligible relative to realtime conversation.
args.security_concerns: Private URLs, extracted snippets, and tab identifiers must remain in the local Mac/job store; relay receives only status and a redacted summary. Device identity, lease epoch, and action idempotency keys must be authenticated. Never replay a non-idempotent browser action after an uncertain result; mark it unknown and surface the exact last action/evidence. Resume should preserve owner policy of no approval gates, while stopping only on transport ambiguity or an actually irreversible submission.
missing: Durable browser job runner with persisted jobId, step checkpoints, retries, and result stream (the existing router is not sufficient).
Lease fencing and quarantine: per-device heartbeat epoch, expiry, attempt cap, and cancellation of processing commands claimed by a device that disappeared; stale results must be rejected.
A browser result journal that records action idempotency key, tab/session affinity, before/after page fingerprint, and unknown-result state, then feeds the Mac planner and pendant alert.
Safari extension reconnect/heartbeat reporting of a stable device identity and tab inventory; currently only tabless home-chrome is online and it is claiming old work.

args.change: Implement browser-command lease fencing and stale-work quarantine. Every command gets a deviceId plus monotonically increasing lease epoch, claimedAt, heartbeat deadline, attempt budget, and terminal outcome (succeeded, failed, expired, quarantined, unknown). /browser/poll may claim only commands whose lease is absent/expired and whose target device matches; a reconnecting device must establish a new epoch before claiming. Results include commandId+epoch+idempotencyKey and are rejected if epoch is stale. On bridge disappearance, atomically quarantine in-flight browser mutations and emit a resumable checkpoint to the job runner instead of requeueing blindly. Add a diagnostic endpoint/dashboard view showing zombie age, claimant, attempts, and reason.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop seeing browser tasks silently hang, get claimed by a tabless device, or repeat clicks after Safari reconnects. Private work can wait safely for the real Safari session, and the owner gets a clear explanation instead of a misleading success or an endless spinner.
args.effort: Medium: schema migration and transaction-safe claim/result paths in browserBridge/browserSessions, extension heartbeat epoch, tests for crash/reconnect races, and a small diagnostic projection.
args.risk: A clock or heartbeat bug could quarantine healthy work and delay it. Recover by allowing explicit lease renewal, bounded expiry, and a planner-visible retry/resume operation; never delete evidence or silently discard the checkpoint.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful model cost; a few D1/local journal writes per command and tiny status payloads.
args.latency_impact: Poll/claim adds one cheap compare-and-set; stale detection is bounded by the heartbeat deadline (30–60s).
args.security_impact: Improves isolation: a stale or wrong device cannot submit a late result for a private tab. Persisted page evidence remains local; device/epoch tokens must be unguessable and authenticated.
depends_on: Stable Safari extension device identity and heartbeat reporting (currently Safari is absent and tabless home-chrome is claiming stale work).
The durable browser job runner/checkpoint store proposed in chg-16bc5dee, or at minimum durable command journal.
Existing idempotency journal and tab/session affinity from chg-14accc01.

args.user_asks: “Tell me the one number I need from the private page I’m looking at, but don’t send the rest of that page anywhere.”
args.why_useful: The browser is uniquely able to see authenticated pages, but today a page read is effectively an all-or-nothing extraction: the owner cannot ask for a single field while guaranteeing that unrelated private content never enters relay context, model prompts, logs, or pendant audio. This would make private browser assistance usable for sensitive finance, health, work, and account pages without turning the whole page into shared context.
args.model_tier: A small local extraction/selector model on the Mac handles DOM targeting and redaction. Use the expensive realtime tier only if the owner asks a spoken follow-up; never send the raw page to it. Background model work is limited to normalizing the requested field and checking confidence.
args.latency_budget: Return a requested scalar or short field in 2–5 seconds for an already-open tab; if semantic targeting is ambiguous, return candidate labels and ask the owner to choose rather than exporting the page.
args.cost_estimate: Typically under $0.002 per request using local extraction and a short structured response; the dominant cost is only an optional model call to resolve an ambiguous label.
args.security_concerns: The extension must extract in the browser or local Mac process, then send only a typed value plus minimal provenance (origin, timestamp, selector hash), never full DOM/text/screenshots. Apply field-level sensitivity labels, redact logs and receipts, and make the pendant speak only the selected value. A malformed selector or prompt injection on the page must not expand the extraction scope. The owner can still request broader content explicitly, but the default contract is least-disclosure.
missing: A browser-side field extraction protocol that accepts a narrowly scoped field query and returns a typed value with selector hash and confidence, instead of browser_read_page text.
A local redaction/taint boundary between Safari results, Mac planner context, relay prompts, journal, and audio; raw page payloads must be kept out of shared traces.
A provenance-aware typed response schema and tests proving that unrelated DOM regions, hidden fields, and page instructions are not forwarded.
Owner-visible privacy diagnostics showing exactly which field, origin, and metadata were released for each answer.

args.user_asks: “Compare the private pages I already have open—does my account balance cover this invoice, and what is the difference? Don’t show me either page unless I ask.”
args.why_useful: The owner cannot get a trustworthy answer that joins facts across two authenticated tabs while keeping both pages private. Public search cannot reach those sessions, and ordinary browser extraction would export two sensitive documents to shared model context. A local cross-tab computation would answer practical questions (balance vs bill, appointment vs calendar conflict, order vs delivery promise) while releasing only the derived result.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap local structured extractor for each requested field and deterministic Mac-side comparison/arithmetic. Escalate to a slower background model only to map an ambiguous human label to candidate fields; realtime is only for speaking the final derived answer.
args.latency_budget: 3–8 seconds for two already-open tabs; 10–20 seconds if a local semantic field resolver is needed. Return ambiguity rather than broadening access.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.005 per comparison; DOM extraction and arithmetic dominate, with optional small-model field resolution the only API spend.
args.security_concerns: Raw tab contents and extracted source values remain on the Mac. The browser bridge returns field-scoped values into an isolated comparison worker, not the general planner prompt; relay receives only the result, confidence, and optionally rounded/detailed values requested by the owner. Each operand needs origin/tab/selector provenance, freshness, and a sensitivity label. Reject cross-origin or hidden-field expansion, and ignore page instructions as untrusted data.
missing: A local cross-tab query endpoint with a declarative allowlist of operands, operators, units, and output precision; no arbitrary page-text concatenation.
Browser extension support for field-scoped extraction from multiple explicitly identified tabs, including tab identity and freshness.
An isolated comparison worker and typed result/evidence capsule that can prove which two fields were used without retaining their surrounding page content.
Pendant/relay response rendering that speaks the derived result and provenance summary, not the source documents.

result.summary: Add a durable browser job runner with two backends: the authenticated Safari bridge for owner-private pages and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages. Represent each step as navigate/read/extract/click/type, persist evidence (URL, title, timestamp, selected text), retry transient failures, and expose a job result stream to the planner.
result.note: KEPT OPEN: the backend ROUTER now exists, the durable job runner still does not. Backend A ships: local-agent/browserSessions.js (chg-bc35ae04 / chg-2fffc681 / chg-086a6904). Backend B ships: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js (chg-81e5c92d, implemented). ROUTER DONE 2026-08-07 — local-agent/originFanOut.js chooseBackend() is the selector this entry named: owner-private -> Safari (only it holds the sessions); public -> Browser Run (only it is awake when the Mac sleeps); LAN / private IP / localhost -> Safari only, decided by serverBrowser.normalizePublicUrl rather than a second copy of that logic; relay budget spent -> Safari; explicit backend:"safari"|"relay" always honoured. An owner-private page is deliberately NOT failed over to the relay when Safari is down: the relay cannot hold the session, so the trip buys a login wall at the price of one of ten daily browser-minutes, and reserving that budget is what keeps the public leg answerable. Free-tier limits are enforced rather than documented: relay lane is serial, paced to 1 action per 10s, and a UTC-day browser-ms tally persists in .pendant-relay-browser-budget.json (GET /origins/budget). MISSING STILL: no durable job runner — no jobId, no persistence across a restart, no retry of transient failures — and no job result stream to the planner. serverBrowser is still unreachable from the voice path (chg-f527c3bc, unapplied wiring diff).

result.summary: Build a first-class authenticated page-watch service: each watch stores URL/tab context, extraction selectors or semantic regions, a normalized baseline hash, volatile-field rules, cadence, and last successful session. On each run, capture a minimal diff with quoted evidence and provenance, publish it as an immutable artifact to the shared task ledger, and notify the relay only when a change crosses the owner's priority threshold. args.subject: Recovery design distinction
args.body: Live /browser/status shows offline=false and pendingCommands=9; sessions persisted but stale. Existing chg-14 only lacks progress/resumable polling; chg-16 durable runner missing. I propose a lease-aware browser reconnect/janitor: TTL + cancellation of queued commands on disconnect/reconnect, classify stale actions, emit diagnostics to Mac/pendant, and resume only idempotent reads. This complements your circuit breaker rather than replacing it.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.change: Add a lease-aware Safari bridge recovery protocol. Every queued browser command gets a device lease, created/expiry timestamps, an action class (read, reversible edit, irreversible), and a cancel token. When extension heartbeats disappear, stop dispatching new commands and move in-flight work to suspended; on reconnect, discard expired or superseded commands (especially type/click), resume only idempotent reads against a verified tab/session, and emit a typed recovery receipt with the exact dropped/resumed command IDs and reason. Add a janitor for the currently observed stale queue (9 pending commands), plus GET diagnostics for heartbeat age, queue age histogram, and last successful tab attachment. Wire recovery receipts into the Mac bridge/pending pendant alert so the owner hears 'Safari returned; 2 reads resumed, 1 stale form fill discarded' instead of waiting through repeated 45-second timeouts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Safari sleep, browser restarts, or laptop network changes will no longer cause old private-page actions to run unexpectedly when the session returns, nor silently lose a requested read. The owner gets a concise explanation and a trustworthy continuation of safe work.
args.effort: Medium: extend browserBridge queue state and persistence, add heartbeat transition handling and janitor, typed receipts, and Mac/relay event plumbing; no extension UI change required beyond existing heartbeat.
args.risk: A false disconnect or tab replacement could suspend useful work or discard an edit. Preserve the command and evidence in a dead-letter journal, expose explicit retry from the owner, and require tab/session identity plus URL match before resuming. Never auto-resume clicks/types after a lease break.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; local JSON/D1 journal growth bounded with 30-day retention. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds a fast heartbeat/lease check; reconnect recovery is immediate for reads, while currently blocked commands stop waiting instead of consuming repeated 45-second timeouts.
args.security_impact: Improves safety for authenticated sessions by preventing stale commands from executing after reconnect. Receipts should contain hashes/URLs and action metadata, not page secrets or form values.

args.change: Add a local-first sensitive-content boundary for authenticated Safari results. Before browser text, snapshots, or form evidence leave the Mac, run DOM-aware redaction for password/OTP/token fields, hidden inputs, credit-card/account-number patterns, and owner-configured selectors; replace values with stable opaque tokens while retaining local-only encrypted evidence keyed by inspection ID. Send the planner only the minimum quoted regions plus URL/title/timestamp and a redaction manifest. If an action needs a redacted value, resolve the token locally in the browser bridge without exposing it to relay logs or the language model, and record only a hash in receipts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely ask about private logged-in pages and prepare forms without passwords, one-time codes, or full account numbers being copied into cloud prompts, journal files, or spoken responses. They get useful answers while reducing accidental secret exposure.
args.effort: Medium-high: DOM extraction/redaction library in browserBridge, encrypted local evidence store and token resolver, configurable selectors, and tests against page text/snapshot/form paths.
args.risk: Over-redaction can make a page summary incomplete; under-redaction can leak a novel secret format. Default to conservative pattern/field redaction, show '[redacted]' markers, allow an explicit local-only inspection mode, and never synthesize or speak redacted values. If the local vault is unavailable, fail closed for sensitive fields but still return nonsensitive text.
args.cost_impact: Small local CPU/storage overhead; no additional model/API calls. Encrypted evidence retention should be capped (for example 7 days or per-job deletion).
args.latency_impact: Typically tens of milliseconds for DOM scan and regex classification; large snapshots may add under 200 ms locally, preferable to sending entire pages for model-side filtering.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces secret exfiltration through relay, logs, receipts, and TTS. Requires OS keychain or an equivalent Mac-local key for the evidence vault, strict token scoping by tab/session, and audit events that contain no raw values.

chg-e14fff33's provenance-aware browser workbench (use hashes/locators, never raw secrets)

transcript.text:
Round 97 findings:

- `/browser/status`: Safari and `home-chrome` are offline; **9 commands remain pending**.
- Persisted sessions still reference three old tabs, but no live extension is reporting a tab.
- `/browser/inspections` is empty.
- Recorded this as a live browser-health finding.

I submitted two new changes:

1. **Lease-aware browser recovery**
   - Suspend commands when Safari disappears.
   - Resume only idempotent reads after reconnect and verified tab/session matching.
   - Expire stale clicks/types, maintain dead-letter receipts, and report what was resumed or discarded.
   - This addresses the current queue of nine stale commands and complements—not duplicates—the durable job-runner proposal.

2. **Local-first sensitive-content boundary**
   - Redact passwords, OTPs, tokens, hidden fields, payment data, and configured sensitive selectors before page content reaches relay prompts, logs, receipts, or TTS.
   - Keep encrypted evidence locally and use opaque tokens when a local browser action needs a redacted value.
   - This lets the owner use authenticated pages without unnecessarily exporting secrets.

What I still need is implementation, not additional authorization:

- A functioning browser command enqueue path; the granted enqueue tools remain schema-only.
- Safari’s extension heartbeat to return, or a reliable reconnect/attach mechanism.
- The durable browser job runner and result stream, which remain open.
- Mac-local encrypted storage/keychain support for the proposed redaction boundary.

I also informed `mac-planner` and `mac-terminal` of the offline state and recovery design.

args.user_asks: “Read this private webpage to me, but hide passwords, codes, account numbers, and other sensitive details. Give me the useful answer through the pendant, and let me ask for one specific redacted detail only when I need it.”
args.why_useful: Today an authenticated page can be inspected or summarized, but sensitive text risks entering prompts, logs, receipts, or spoken output, while a blanket redaction would make the answer unusable. This gives the owner a practical privacy-preserving way to use logged-in Safari pages from the pendant: useful content is spoken immediately, secrets stay on the Mac, and narrowly requested disclosures remain local and deliberate.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background/local extraction model on the Mac to classify and summarize page regions; use the realtime tier only for the owner's live spoken request and short response. Never send redacted values to the cloud model.
args.latency_budget: Initial page capture and local redaction under 1 second for ordinary pages; spoken response within 2–3 seconds. A specific local-only reveal can take up to 1 second.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental API cost for extraction because it runs locally; one short realtime turn for the spoken interaction. Dominant cost is existing audio relay/TTS, not page analysis.
args.security_concerns: Passwords, OTPs, tokens, hidden inputs, payment data, and configured private selectors must be redacted before any page text leaves the Mac. Store sensitive spans only in an encrypted, short-lived Mac-local vault keyed to tab/session and inspection ID. A requested reveal must resolve locally and never be written to relay logs, cloud prompts, receipts, or durable memory. The owner should be able to disable all reveals.
missing: A Mac-local DOM-aware redaction and encrypted evidence vault
A typed browser result format carrying opaque sensitive-span tokens and safe quoted evidence
A local-only reveal operation bound to the current tab/session and owner request
Pendant response plumbing that can play the safe summary and accept a follow-up request

args.user_asks: “If I’m looking at a private page, let me tap the pendant to get one sensitive field read back privately, without putting that field into the cloud, browser history, or action logs.”
args.why_useful: The owner sometimes needs a single order number, access code, or account detail from a logged-in page while away from the screen. Today the system either exposes page text broadly to software or cannot safely provide the detail at all. A short-lived pendant-bound disclosure gives useful access without turning the browser into a secret-export channel.
args.model_tier: No model should interpret or retain the secret. The Mac performs deterministic local DOM extraction and selector/pattern matching; realtime handles only the spoken request and a confirmation-free acknowledgment, never the value.
args.latency_budget: Tap-to-result under 1.5 seconds while Safari is connected; if the tab or bridge is unavailable, fail clearly without queuing the secret request.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API/model cost; local extraction and one short audio response dominate. Small encrypted local cache, automatically erased after one successful playback or 60 seconds.
args.security_concerns: Require physical pendant presence plus a fresh session-bound nonce, but do not make this a general action-approval gate. Resolve only one field from the currently bound tab, never arbitrary page text; mask the value in all logs and receipts; do not allow replay, relay-side caching, or transcription. The pendant should indicate when a sensitive value is being spoken, and the owner can disable the feature.
missing: Pendant firmware support for a short-lived secure-presence nonce and private-disclosure indicator
A Mac-local browser resolver that maps an owner phrase or configured selector to exactly one sensitive field without sending its value to any model
An end-to-end encrypted, memory-only result channel from Mac to pendant audio
Redaction-aware receipts that record only field type, tab/session, and outcome

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

1. **Privacy-preserving private-page reading**
   - The pendant receives a useful summary of the logged-in Safari page.
   - Passwords, OTPs, tokens, payment data, and other sensitive fields stay local.
   - Specific redacted details can be resolved locally without sending them to cloud prompts, logs, or durable memory.

2. **Pendant-bound single-field disclosure**
   - A physical pendant tap requests one sensitive field from the currently bound private tab.
   - The value travels only through an encrypted Mac-to-pendant path, expires immediately, and is absent from logs and receipts.
   - It requires new pendant nonce/presence support, local browser field resolution, and memory-only secure audio delivery.

args.subject: Browser continuity proposal
args.body: Live browser is offline, 9 pending commands; sessions are stale but persisted (default tab 320512 time.is). I’m proposing a novel browser→Mac handoff envelope: field-level redaction + provenance + expiring one-shot capability token, so Mac can act on minimal authenticated facts without raw DOM/session leakage; include stale-session reconciliation on reconnect.

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.change: Add a privacy-preserving browser-to-fleet handoff envelope. After an authenticated Safari extraction, the browser harness emits only the requested fields (not raw DOM, cookies, or screenshots), each with tab/session id, URL, timestamp, locator/snippet hash, confidence, and an expiry. Sign it with a one-shot capability token scoped to the exact downstream operation (for example, create a reminder or draft text on the Mac); the Mac/relay can redeem it once, then it is invalidated. On extension reconnect, reconcile pending commands against these envelopes and mark stale tab-bound commands expired rather than replaying them.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask the pendant about a private logged-in page and have the Mac follow up without silently copying an entire sensitive page into model context or accidentally replaying an old browser action after Safari was offline. Results remain evidence-backed and narrowly scoped while still enabling genuinely cross-device workflows.
args.effort: Medium: extend browserBridge/browserSessions result schema and durable queue, add field-selection/redaction and token store, add Mac-side redemption plus reconnect reconciliation, and expose receipt events in the existing jobs/inspections dashboard.
args.risk: A bad selector or overly broad field request could omit context or disclose more than intended; token loss could leave a job incomplete. Default to explicit requested-field manifests, short TTLs, hash-only provenance, and retry as a fresh read after expiry. Never replay a mutation from a stale envelope; existing receipt/undo remains available for reversible Mac actions.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost beyond the extraction/planner call already required; small D1/R2 metadata growth (roughly 1–3 KB per handoff, with TTL cleanup).
args.latency_impact: Adds about 10–30 ms for signing/storage and one local redemption round trip; no extra model call.
args.security_impact: Improves isolation: raw authenticated page content stays in the browser boundary, downstream receives least-privilege fields and an expiring one-use token. Still requires careful redaction of snippets and strict audit logging of redemption.
